Game changesWiki changes

Source history through 13 October 2026 · 5856103c. These are commit dates, not numbered releases. Coverage and limits.

Before updating

Compatibility at the reviewed revision. See also Saves and world files and Building.

  • Compatibility · Save files

    At the reviewed game revision, saves are written as format 29 and formats 10–29 are accepted. Format 28 widened stored block IDs; format 29 stores survival milestones. Keep a separate copy of your world before trying an older build: there is no downgrade conversion.

    Source commits
    • 208a24f1 · 13 October 2026
    • 1363b0c8 · 13 October 2026

  • Compatibility · Older terrain

    Saves before format 10 predate the half-metre grid and are refused, not converted. Supported saved worlds retain their generator selection; updating the game does not turn an old world into the newest terrain generation.

    Source commits
    • bc28842b · 26 September 2026
    • 1363b0c8 · 13 October 2026

  • Compatibility · Multiplayer

    The reviewed client and server use protocol 16. Protocol and terrain/build checks can refuse a mismatched peer, so update both ends together. The LAN features described here do not imply full shared survival or public-internet readiness.

    Source commits
    • 4c8170fc · 4 October 2026
    • 6dd7dbc9 · 4 October 2026
    • 7d2e80ef · 13 October 2026
    • 5f1052e6 · 13 October 2026

  • Compatibility · Structure workshop

    New flat workshops are separate saves. Elevated workshops remain in Worlds as legacy workshops with their builds intact. Move a build through the Blueprint library and check the copy before removing the original.

    Source commit
    • f8dec3b5 · 12 October 2026

  • Compatibility · Blueprint files

    The reviewed blueprint format is version 1 and records blocks by stable name. Doors are excluded from captures. Newer or unknown content can be refused; the world-save format number is not the blueprint format number.

    Source commits
    • 99cc8a68 · 12 October 2026
    • 5d4d87c3 · 12 October 2026
    • 208a24f1 · 13 October 2026

13 October 2026

Milestones, shared doors and safer saves

  • Added · Survival

    Fifteen saved survival milestones appear on an inventory tab. Follow-up fixes make previously unreachable milestones attainable and give their announcements a separate line.

    Source commits
    • 1363b0c8 · 13 October 2026
    • 2596d051 · 13 October 2026

  • Changed · Save compatibility

    Format 28 stores wider block identifiers; format 29 then adds milestone progress. The reviewed build reads formats 10–29 and writes 29. An older build cannot read a save written in a newer format.

    Source commits
    • 208a24f1 · 13 October 2026
    • 1363b0c8 · 13 October 2026

  • Changed · Network compatibility

    Protocol 15 carries wider block identifiers; protocol 16 adds hanging, swinging and removing doors on servers. Use matching client and server builds.

    Source commits
    • 7d2e80ef · 13 October 2026
    • 5f1052e6 · 13 October 2026

  • Added · Multiplayer

    The menu lists worlds hosted on the local network. Other players’ punches, mining strokes and placements become visible, and remote door swings animate instead of snapping.

    Source commits
    • f8cdb531 · 13 October 2026
    • 46ef04ba · 13 October 2026
    • c20231d7 · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Saving

    Hosted saves wait for disk completion and show failures. They retain the owner’s rest point and settle pending edits before saving. Save publication syncs the containing directory and rejects oversized saves before writing.

    Source commits
    • 146d4f82 · 13 October 2026
    • 55d524d6 · 13 October 2026
    • 41908f28 · 13 October 2026
    • 763d0455 · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Destinations and home

    Removing Journal pins preserves unrelated destinations. A missing hosted destination no longer makes the save unloadable, and lost home-crate repair uses a dry supported site.

    Source commits
    • c22f84a8 · 13 October 2026
    • 19705adb · 13 October 2026
    • b70d279a · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Doors

    Swings wait for their leaves to be drawn. Respawns, reloads and undo avoid open leaves; door placement checks players and animals. A server refusal restores the whole door.

    Source commits
    • 4e4d908f · 13 October 2026
    • 1c6dc40a · 13 October 2026
    • f6dde4ca · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Crafting and mining

    X repeats the recipe selected on the Craft tab instead of spending resources on the first affordable recipe. Mining blows chip the struck face and cracks advance as the block is worked.

    Source commits
    • a6d56495 · 13 October 2026
    • 65a0f51f · 13 October 2026
    • 4147f194 · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Drinking and projectiles

    The drinking line checks each crossed voxel, including diagonal obstructions. A throw or shot that cannot launch keeps its item or ammunition. Projectile rest is determined by speed rather than a single step’s distance.

    Source commits
    • da52f269 · 13 October 2026
    • a9d24cec · 13 October 2026

  • Changed · Camera and held items

    Newly equipped items rise into view. Disabling View bob also stills walking sway. Speed FOV and damage dips use real frame time, keeping their pace below 20 FPS.

    Source commits
    • 301e28f6 · 13 October 2026
    • 5856103c · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Menus and pictures

    World and structure searches share Unicode-aware case folding, structure updates find the exact existing file, and world pictures move off the frame’s GPU wait and disk-writing path. Item icon tiles stand upright.

    Source commits
    • ee5ffbb0 · 13 October 2026
    • 5bd2b06f · 13 October 2026
    • 51dc8961 · 13 October 2026
    • a3e6f464 · 13 October 2026
    • 6b528554 · 13 October 2026

  • Fixed · Streaming and joining

    Generation and map-detail workers recover from panics; synchronous generation fallback is bounded. Silent server addresses cannot each consume the whole join deadline.

    Source commits
    • 05b740d8 · 13 October 2026
    • fb2dea33 · 13 October 2026
    • 669db134 · 13 October 2026
    • 9237a430 · 13 October 2026
    • 70fcc43e · 13 October 2026

30 September 2026

Longer horizons and steadier streaming

  • Changed · Rendering

    Terrain streaming reuses outgoing meshes and cancels obsolete work. Detail selection uses three-dimensional distance; fixes cover surface transitions, ice, cactus joins and excavated structures. Lag reports and runtime effort charts help diagnose slow frames.

  • Added · Horizon

    A saved 512-chunk horizon option extends the distant view to roughly 8 km. Remote terrain keeps coverage while changing detail, and wildlife spawning waits for resident terrain to avoid generation spikes.

Coverage and sources

Dates are Git committer dates in each commit’s recorded timezone, not release or download dates. Every available commit subject in the pinned intervals was reviewed; summaries group related base-game changes, with source and patch checks for compatibility and controls. This is a source-history review, not a new gameplay test.

First recorded commit
16 August 2026 · 6c39b717820ae80f3fd369fdcc406f693bdc8652
Reviewed through
13 October 2026 · 5856103c4d15fd12a2118e72d0b51bbb9f074895
Available history
704 commits; 17 dated groups shown.

Game commit identifiers come from the checked source repository. Its hosted history was unavailable to a public request during review, so these identifiers are shown without public links. Compatibility was checked in the save loader, blueprint codec and network protocol at the reviewed revision.

  • The game history starts with a large snapshot on 16 August 2026. Earlier development and changes between recorded snapshots cannot be dated more precisely.
  • There are no tags in either inspected checkout. The public game release endpoint returned 404 during review, so game releases could not be verified. The wiki release endpoint returned an empty list. No release numbers are inferred from package metadata.
  • Optional content, internal refactors, test-only changes and development plans are omitted. Some recorded days therefore have no entry. Broad early snapshots can only support grouped summaries.
  • Wiki history begins with the standalone import on 9 October. Older atlas capture dates describe preserved media, not earlier commits in this repository.
  • The cutoff is explicit below. Later commits are not covered until the next review; this chronology does not refresh the dates or receipts in older guides and galleries.
